title: Research page: where the book chapters go
thesis: Sixteen entries still fit on one page, so nothing needs to move to a second page. What needs to change is the order and the signposting: published work first, the chapters in their own section, and a row at the top that says what kinds of work the page holds and how many of each.

measured.how: the live felipemaffonso.com/research/ with every entry closed, Chrome at 1280 x 902 and at 390 x 844 (an iPhone 14)

pick.headline: My pick: option B, and keep the name Research.
reasons: Sixteen entries are about two screens on a laptop and three on a phone. That is not bloated, and a list of 25 would not be either, because every entry stays one to three lines until someone opens it. A second page would only make visitors click to find out what you have.
Today a visitor sees three preprints before the first published paper, and on a phone the Journal Publications heading sits at the bottom of the first screen. Published work should come first.

The row of buttons with counts tells a visitor what is on the page and how much before they scroll, which is the signal you asked about. A search committee member can tap Journal publications and see only those. A Books button appears by itself the day a book is added.

Keep Research as the menu name. It sits next to Teaching, which also names an activity, and it covers preprints, which are not publications yet. Changing it also changes the page title Google shows, and moving the address would need a forwarding page so old links keep working.

You do not need shadcn. The site does not use shadcn components; the button row would be written in the site's own styles (the same coral, borders and type) and would behave like shadcn's toggle group: arrow keys move between buttons and screen readers announce which one is on. No new package.

options.name: Today, with the chapters added at the bottom
options.what: Only the two chapters are added, as a third section under the journal publications. Nothing else changes.
good: Visitors who know the page find it unchanged.
cost: Three preprints still come before any published paper.
The chapters sit at the very bottom, under eleven articles, where few visitors scroll.
Nothing at the top says the page also has chapters.

options.name: Published work first, with a jump line
options.what: Journal publications, then book chapters, then preprints. One line under the title names the three kinds with their counts, and each name jumps to its section.
good: The smallest change after adding the chapters.
Published work is the first thing anyone sees.
The counts say what is below.
cost: The line scrolls away with the page.
There is no way to see only one kind.

options.name: Published work first, with a filter row
options.what: A row of buttons under the title: All, Journal publications, Book chapters, Preprints, each with its count. All shows every section in order; a button shows only that kind. The row stays under the menu bar while you scroll.
good: The counts say what is on the page before anyone scrolls.
One tap narrows the list to what a visitor came for.
A Books button appears by itself when the first book is added.
Works the same on a phone, where it is one line tall.
cost: One more element at the top of the page.
On a phone the row takes one line of the screen while you scroll.
Once a Books button is added, the row on a phone is slightly wider than the screen and scrolls sideways (try the book preview above).

options.name: Publications, newest first, grouped by year
options.what: The page is renamed Publications. Everything is listed newest first under year headings, with a small tag saying what each entry is. Preprints go last because they have no year. The filter row narrows by kind.
good: Shows a steady record over the years.
The tags make a chapter easy to tell from an article.
cost: Renaming changes the menu, the page title and possibly the address.
The year headings split the eleven articles into six small groups.
The Forthcoming group mixes articles and chapters, so the most important work is not grouped by kind.

options.name: Published work first, with a side index
options.what: On a laptop, a narrow list on the left names each section with its count and highlights the section you are reading. On a phone it becomes a row of buttons at the top.
good: Grows well if the page later adds books, reports or talks.
cost: The most code of the five.
The page is too short today to need it.
It changes the page from one column to two on a laptop.
